figures.caption: Figure 1: Schematic comparison of three reasoning paradigms: (a) Explicit CoT Reasoning, (b) Latent Reasoning, and (c) our Factorized Latent Reasoning (FLR).

Figure 4: Visualization of factor disentanglement on Toys and Games datasets. (a, c) Unconstrained Setting: Latent factors exhibit high redundancy (Avg |Corr| ≈ 0.44), indicating mode collapse. (b, d) With FLR Constraints: Factors become highly orthogonal and independent (Avg |Corr| ≈ 0.03), validating the efficacy of the proposed regularization.

Figure 5: Relative performance improvement of LR-GRPO and FLR-GRPO over the FLR baseline. The comparison is conducted across four datasets (Toys, CDs, Games, Instruments) in terms of HR@K and NDCG@K. The baseline (0%) represents the performance of the FLR model.
Figure 2: Illustration of the FLR architecture and its Two-Stage training paradigm.
Figure 3: Illustration of the Factorized Latent Reasoning (FLR) module.
Table 4: Impact of our GRPO Strategies. Specifically, LRGRPO is the improvedGRPOmethod fromLatentR3, whereas FLR-GRPO is our proposed RL approach.
Table 3: Ablation study results on Games and Toys datasets. "None" represents the FLR model without any regularization constraints (L𝑜𝑟𝑡ℎ,L𝑑𝑖𝑣,L𝑠𝑝𝑎𝑟𝑠𝑒 ). Bold values denote the best results.

Figure 6: Visualization of attention patterns on Amazon Video Games. The x-axis shows recommended items, and the y-axis shows latent attention heads. (a) The pre-trained baseline exhibits redundant attention. (b) FLR-GRPO demonstrates categoryaware specialization.
